correctness.rationale: For two normalized symmetric opinion equations d’=-2w*phi(d)*d/(1+w), w’=w(1-w)(2phi(d)-1), with C2 decreasing positive phi crossing one half transversely at r_c∈(0,2), the exact integral H(d)=∫(2phi-1)/(2d phi) dd gives invariant C=atanh(w)+H(d). H has maximum 0 at r_c and diverges negatively near zero; this yields the exact threshold w_c=tanh[-H(d0)] for d0>r_c, polarization for weaker ties, critical d→r_c and w→0, consensus otherwise. Taylor H≈phi’(r_c)(d-r_c)^2/r_c proves t(d-r_c)→1/(-phi’(r_c)) and t^2 w→1/[r_c(-phi’(r_c))]. Independent numerical integrations on both sides of the boundary confirmed invariant conservation and phase outcomes; limiting exponents derive analytically.
